concept.name: Public key
concept.definition: A public key is the openly shareable half of an account's cryptographic key pair, derived one-way from the private key and used by the network to verify signatures and derive the account address.
concept.intuition: It is like your email address for money: anyone can know it and send you funds, but only the matching private key can spend them.
concept.mechanics: The public key is computed from the private key by elliptic-curve multiplication, which is infeasible to reverse. On Ethereum, the account address is the last 20 bytes of the Keccak-256 hash of the public key; when a signed transaction is broadcast, nodes recover the public key from the signature to prove the sender's identity.
concept.formula: public_key = private_key × G (one-way elliptic curve multiplication); address = last 20 bytes of Keccak256(public_key), prefixed with 0x.
concept.failure_modes: Sharing a public key or address is safe for receiving funds, but address reuse and public on-chain history destroy privacy since anyone can trace all associated activity.
concept.misconceptions: A public key is not the same as an address — the address is a hash of the public key, and the public key itself is only revealed on-chain when the account first sends a transaction.
concept.example: An Ethereum address such as 0x5e97870f263700f46aa00d967821199b9bc5a120 is derived by hashing the account's public key; anyone can verify that a transaction signed by the matching private key genuinely came from that account.
